proof_summary: Both 56 and 60 are divisible by \(2^2\), so the original encoding treats them as the distinct values 56 and 60, whereas factorization gives \(A003415=92\), gcd value 4, and exactly two divisors of the form \(k^k\), yielding the same triple \((92,4,2)\). Since every input free of divisors \(p^p\) has \(A376418=1\), the triple encoding is a quotient of the original one; the collision merges two classes by \(n=60\), so the restricted-growth values differ there.
